H&P – Detailed

Consult Summary:
27-year-old male with 6-week history of left-sided reduced hearing, intermittent tinnitus, and mild disequilibrium; no pain or discharge. Plan is face-to-face otoscopic assessment to rule out cerumen impaction; tinnitus information provided.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Progressive reduction in hearing in the left ear.  
• Onset & duration: Began ~6 weeks ago; intermittent since onset.  
• Progression: Ongoing, not resolved; previously experienced a brief (couple-day) episode one year ago.  
• Associated symptoms:  
  – Intermittent ringing (tinnitus) in left ear, triggered by external sound (e.g., TV, music).  
  – Mild, non-rotatory dizziness/“off balance”; no true vertigo, nausea, or vomiting.  
• Negative symptoms: No ear pain, no otorrhea, no fever, no chest pain, no palpitations, no pruritus.  
• Exacerbating/relieving factors: Sound exposure precipitates tinnitus; no other modifiers described.  
• Systems review: otherwise non-contributory; right ear normal per patient.

Past Medical History:
• None mentioned.

Medications:
• None mentioned.  
Allergies:
• Not discussed.

Social History:
• Not discussed (smoking, alcohol, substance use, occupation not documented).

Family History:
• Not discussed.

Physical Examination:
• No physical examination performed during video consult; vitals not obtained.

Investigations:
• None performed. Plan for otoscopic examination at in-person clinic visit.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Left-sided hearing loss ± cerumen impaction
  – Arrange face-to-face appointment within 4–5 days for otoscopic evaluation to assess for impacted wax or other external/middle-ear pathology.

Issue 2: Tinnitus
  – Patient educated that symptom is called tinnitus; etiology often multifactorial and not fully understood.  
  – Provide patient with educational leaflet (link pasted into visit notes) to review prior to in-person visit.

Issue 3: Mild disequilibrium
  – Acknowledge symptom; will re-assess once otoscopic findings available and hearing issue addressed.  
  – No red-flag features (no vertigo, chest pain, palpitations) at present.

General Plan items:
• Administrative: Clinician to message admin team to schedule clinic slot; patient instructed to call support team to confirm.  
• Safety-netting: If symptoms worsen or new concerns arise before appointment, patient to book another video consult.  
• Follow-up: In-person GP review in 4–5 days; further management contingent on ear examination findings.

Quality checks (document_quality):
• Missing elements: Medications list, drug allergies, vitals, full systems review, social and family history—all not elicited in transcript.  
• Internal conflicts: None noted.  
• Transcript quality: Clear audio; occasional minor overlaps, does not affect data extraction.
